liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Long, lusty jam that leads into an extraordinary transition into Morning Dew; Praised as outstanding, with the Morning Dew that follows also strong [7][12][13]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer finds this version beautiful [13]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Welcome addition to a typical late-72 first set, since Jerry brought the song back a few weeks earlier [4]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 review): At the very end, Keith picks out a Guys And Dolls tune just before Tennessee Jed begins [14]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Reviewer describes it as long and spacy [4]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer hears a cello-like string lead the slither into Dew, with Phil close behind; the Dew itself is monstrous [7]
- **Sing Me Back Home** (1 review): Reviewer calls it well done [10]

## The recordings

- **gd72-08-24.sbd.miller.18093.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 201 min; rated 4.53/5 by 30 [1]
- **gd1972-08-24.156469.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 203 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Restoration was done on the start of Sing Me Back Home, which has issues in every circulating source [2]
- **gd1972-08-24.sbd.unknown.151.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 186 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Slight digital noise over the first line of Sing Me Back Home [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this show displaces 8/21 in their personal top ten [4]
- Often overlooked because the Oregon show came a few days later; reviewer says the band is in peak form here [5]
- Reviewer ranks it the best of the Berkeley shows played after returning from Europe [6]
- Reviewer rates the 24th and 21st above the 27th [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-08-24.sbd.miller.18093.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard to reel-to-reel master to DAT at 48k; missing songs patched from a cassette-generation soundboard lineage, via Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1972-08-24.156469.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: transferred by Mastered by Jamie Waddell and  Jim Blackwood Pitch correction by Jason Chastain Listening assistance, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Master SBD Reel > DAT from ANON [2]. Also: Sugar Magnolia, Greatest Story Ever Told and Ramble On Rose come from the first source lacking extra analog generations; Some tuning came from source 18093; this FLAC release aired on Radio Valenica in March 2022 [2]
- **gd1972-08-24.sbd.unknown.151.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Unknown; source: SBD > ? [3]. Also: Files came from CD-Rs burned from the circulating DAT soundboard; nothing else is known about its descent [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Berkeley Community Theatre, Berkeley, CA. August 1972, three shows. (SBD)](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/10/grateful-dead-berkeley-community.html) [17]
- Fan art by arizjones.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead, Berkeley Community Theatre, Berkeley, CA. August 1972, three shows. (SBD)](https://arizjones.blogspot.com/2015/10/grateful-dead-berkeley-community.html) [18]
